glosses: To join (to another object): to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to another object.

examples.text: I think this piece connects to that piece over there.

glosses: To join: to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to each other.

examples.text: Both roads have the same name, but they don't connect: they're on opposite sides of the river, and there's no bridge there.

examples.text: When that roundhouse kick connected with his temple it sent him flying across the room.

examples.text: The new railroad will connect the northern part of the state to the southern part.

glosses: To join (two other objects), or to join (one object) to (another object): to take one object and attach it to another.

examples.text: I connected the printer to the computer, but I couldn't get it work.

glosses: To join an electrical or telephone line to a circuit or network.

examples.text: When the technician connects my house, I'll be able to access the internet.

glosses: To associate; to establish a relation between.

examples.text: I didn't connect my lost jewelry with the news of an area cat burglar until the police contacted me.

examples.text: I'm flying to London where I connect with a flight heading to Hungary.
